instructions: Cut the 2 1/2 lbs veal into 1 1/2 inch cubes if it isn't already. Put it in a large pot, cover it with cold water and bring it to a boil over high heat. Boil it for 3 minutes, skimming off the gray foam.

Meanwhile, peel the onion and push the 4 cloves into it. Halve the 2 carrots lengthwise and cut them into 2 inch pieces. Cut 2 of the celery ribs into 3 inch pieces. Peel and halve the 3 garlic cloves.
Drain the veal in a colander and rinse it under cold water. Rinse out the pot.

Put the veal back in the pot with the onion, carrots, celery, garlic, 4 parsley stalks, 2 thyme sprigs, the bay leaf and the 1 tsp peppercorns. Add the 8 cups broth, 1 tsp of the salt and the 1/2 tsp white pepper.

Bring it to a boil, then turn the heat to medium-low and simmer gently with the lid ajar for 1 1/2 hours, until a piece of veal is tender enough to cut with a fork. Skim off any foam that rises in the first 10 minutes.

About 30 minutes before the veal is done, rinse the 1 1/2 cups rice and put it in a saucepan with 2 1/4 cups water. Bring it to a boil, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 18 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave it covered.
Meanwhile, slice the mushrooms and squeeze the lemon. That should be about 3 tbsp juice.

Melt 2 tbsp of the butter in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms, 1 cup of the pearl onions straight from the freezer and 1/4 tsp of the salt. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the mushrooms are browned and the onions are golden.
Add the 1/4 cup wine and 1 tbsp of the lemon juice and let it bubble for 2 minutes, until it's almost gone. Take the pan off the heat.

When the veal is tender, lift the veal and carrots into a bowl with a slotted spoon. Strain the broth through a sieve into a large bowl and throw out the onion, celery, garlic and herbs. Measure out 4 cups of the broth and keep the rest for soup.
Wipe out the pot and set it over medium heat. Melt the remaining 3 tbsp butter, then whisk in the 3 tbsp flour. Keep whisking for about 1 1/2 minutes, until it smells nutty but is still pale.
Slowly whisk in 2 cups of the measured broth until it's smooth. Whisk in the other 2 cups, the 3/4 cup cream and the remaining 2 tbsp lemon juice.
Simmer it for about 15 minutes, whisking often, until it has reduced by about half and coats the back of a spoon.
Add the veal, carrots, mushrooms and onions and stir for 3 to 4 minutes, until it's all hot through.
Taste it. If it's flat, add the last 1/4 tsp salt.
Chop 2 tbsp of the parsley leaves. Serve the blanquette over the rice, with the parsley on top.
method_notes: All three simmer cubed veal shoulder gently in liquid with onion, carrots and herbs without browning it, then turn the cooking liquid into a pale sauce and serve it over rice. Club Foody (the lead) blanches the veal first, simmers it in chicken broth with a clove-studded onion, celery and a bouquet garni, makes a butter and flour roux sauce with cream and lemon, and adds mushrooms and pearl onions; Mad About Macarons thickens with egg yolks and crème fraîche instead, and Go Healthy With Bea keeps it to a starch-thickened broth with carrots. This follows the lead but browns the mushrooms and frozen pearl onions together in one pan in place of its separate mushroom and glazed onion steps, and leaves out its optional cornstarch thickener and the bacon fat.
